To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) orthogonalizing the gradients in projected gradient descent can improve adversarial example generation and (b) orthogonalizing the gradient in the projected gradient descent attack can improve adversarial examples' ability to evade detection defenses.

(1) existing attacks that attempt simultaneous constraint satisfaction often over-optimize for one constraint at the expense of the other; (2) we introduce Selective Project Gradient Descent and OPGD, improved attack techniques that avoid this problem; (3) we use our technique to generate adversarial attacks that evade four state-ofthe-art detection defenses, and reduce their accuracy to 100% while maintaining a detection rate of 0%.

(1) existing defenses against adversarial examples are vulnerable to gradient-based attacks, (2) orthogonalizing gradients can evade these attacks, and (3) orthogonalizing gradients is a generalizable technique that can improve adversarial example generation in other contexts.
